label: Kestrel (large hobby, G80T-11)
description: Generic large sport rocket: 41.6 mm (BT-60 size) body, 29 mm motor mount, cardboard and plywood construction, AeroTech G80T-11, 30 in chute on the 11 s motor ejection charge.

notes.mass: 400 g airframe: ~1 m of 41.6 mm tube, plywood fins, payload bay, 30 in nylon chute and 29 mm mount (a 320 g first draft was light for this size and over-flew comparable G-motor sport rockets, which typically reach ~760-1070 m)
notes.cd: 0.60: larger, smoother airframe than the small kits
notes.recovery: single 30 in chute: ~0.5 kg descends at ~5 m/s
notes.rail: 1.5 m rod/rail for a G motor (higher rail-exit speed needed)
notes.delay: 11 s (within the G80T's listed 6-14 s): true apogee comes 11.1 s after burnout; a 7 s delay opened the chute ~4 s early at ~42 m/s

notes.backup_timer_s: nominal true apogee + max(1.0 s, 4 sigma of the apogee time under the standard dispersions), from lift-off; the C6 value 8.5 s follows the same rule (7.42 + 1.08)
notes.max_boost_s: longest burn x 1.6 (C6: 1.86 s -> 3.0 s): burnout fallback for a stuck accelerometer
notes.min_deploy_after_launch_s: final burnout x 1.35 (C6: 1.86 s -> 2.5 s): deploy inhibit
notes.basis: G80T burn 1.70 s; true apogee 13.09 s (sigma 0.24 s); peak ~21 g
notes.motor: SIL flies a 13 s delay (listed range 6-14 s) so the charge fires at 14.7 s, after the FC's apogee event and its 14.1 s backup timer
notes.powered_jerk_psd: 1e4 m^2/s^5 under thrust and for 0.5 s after each detected burnout (tail-off): the coast q (10) cannot follow thrust-curve and tail-off jerk on this rocket, the gate then rejected genuine samples and nominal flights went 'inconsistent' (found by the fleet SIL runs; see fc/include/fc/config.hpp). 1e4 sits in the measured plateau: apogee detection +0.04-0.05 s on every preset
